deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is one of Grothendieck's 1983-84 working notes on 'systèmes de pseudo-droites', roughly configurations of pseudo-lines in the projective plane. He studies the combinatorial space X of relative positions ('positions relatives', abbreviated 'p.r.'). X is stratified by specialisation and generalisation: a generic position specialises to a degenerate one, for instance a 'superposition' or a triple-point configuration, and generalises back. On the previous page and this one he tries to build a space over X, written 𝒳 → X, by gluing local pieces ('recollements').

The local pieces. To each degenerate configuration D he attaches a local model ω_D. Think of it as the small circle or star of generalisations of D, made of arcs, each arc being a generalisation or specialisation direction. Wherever D specialises to or generalises from a neighbour D', a transition isomorphism ω_D → ω_{D'} must be chosen.

The two earlier families of choices. Families A and B on the previous pages fix the gluing combinatorially. In them, α is matched to a or a′, while β is always matched to b. 'Antipodisme', mentioned on the previous page, suggests that orientation or antipodal data enter the arcs.

Case 3 (this page). The gluing is now forced by a 'lien' (link). That is, the isomorphism α ≃ β is the one obtained by transport along a composite of isomorphisms. Equivalently, the transition ω(D) → ω(D′) is parallel transport. A canonical connection on the local data thus determines 𝒳 → X. Two subcases remain.

(1) α = a′. The generalisation at D′ is made along the arc facing ('qui fait face à') the specialisation arc at D. Grothendieck says he had already seen and discarded this case. Rereading, he realises he discarded it because it produces intuitively absurd circuits: from a p.r. near a superposition D, the circuit moves away from D instead of turning around it.

(2) α = a. This is the original case: generalisation along the arc obtained from the specialisation arc by parallel transport. He is convinced that a p.r. cannot be 'joined' by two operations whose states differ in a way not accounted for by 'turning around a hole (or commutation)'.

The criterion. The criterion for a correct gluing is the monodromy of circuits in 𝒳 around codimension-2 degenerations ('trous', i.e. superposition positions). Good circuits wind around the hole; trivial commutations are the other admissible kind.

What follows. A crossed-out comparison of the variants B1, B2, A1, A2 ends the page. On the next page he 'verifies' that A1, A2 and B2 give the right circuits around a superposition position, and that A2, then A1, is the most interesting.

Purpose. In modern terms, this is the search for the right 2-dimensional cell structure, or covering, on the space or poset of pseudo-line arrangements. The 1-cells are elementary moves, or flips. The 2-cells are the circuits around codimension-2 degenerations: commutation squares, and the loops around multiple or superposed points. One wants a 2-complex whose fundamental group or covering correctly encodes the 'turning around a hole' relations, by analogy with Salvetti-type complexes and the Manin–Schechtman higher Bruhat orders.
errors: No mathematical error can be confirmed. The page is an exploratory case analysis, and Grothendieck himself flags that he had mis-dismissed or mis-recalled case 1.
The next page admits several errors during the verification ('pas mal d'erreurs encore dans le cours de la vérification'), so the case conclusions here are provisional.

ideas.what: Gluing local generalisation stars ω_D along specialisation arrows, with transition isomorphisms given by 'parallel transport', to form a space 𝒳 → X over the space of relative positions of pseudo-lines.
ideas.modern_name: Construction of a stratified space or regular CW-complex (a Salvetti-type complex or covering) from the face poset of the stratification of pseudo-line arrangement space; local systems on an exit-path category.
ideas.usually_credited_to: Salvetti (1987) for arrangement complexes; MacPherson / Treumann / Lurie for exit-path categories; Goodman–Pollack and Ringel for pseudo-line arrangement spaces.
ideas.where_published: Possibly echoed in passing in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), which mentions the study of pseudo-line systems and a 'géométrie modérée'; no detailed published account known.

ideas.what: Using circuits 'turning around a hole' (around a codimension-2 superposition position) versus commutations as the test of whether a gluing is correct.
ideas.modern_name: 2-cells and relations of the flip graph (Ringel's homotopy theorem); local monodromy around codimension-2 strata; higher Bruhat order relations (Manin–Schechtman).

ideas.what: Comparison of gluing variants A1, A2, B1, B2 and the 'lien' case 3 with subcases α = a′ and α = a.
ideas.modern_name: Choice of connection or descent datum for a combinatorial covering.

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks a canonical 'parallel transport' gluing of local generalisation data over the stratified space of pseudo-line configurations. He tests it by the requirement that loops near a degenerate (superposition) configuration wind around it rather than escape. This is an attempt to define the correct 2-type or covering of the moduli space of pseudo-line arrangements. The thread is unfinished, and the literature on pseudo-line and oriented-matroid realisation spaces did not take up this geometric-covering viewpoint in his form.
missed.quote: en partant d'une p.r. proche d'une superposition, D, on s'écarte de D au lieu de tourner autour comme on devrait normalement
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects to the homotopy type of spaces of pseudo-line arrangements and oriented-matroid Grassmannians (MacPhersonians, Anderson–Davis), and to higher Bruhat orders. A local-monodromy criterion of this type could inform cellular models of those spaces. The page is too fragmentary to extract a definite result, however.

deep.surprise_reason: Interesting as a trace of Grothendieck's little-known pseudo-line programme, and it anticipates monodromy and cell-structure questions later studied via Salvetti complexes and higher Bruhat orders. The page itself is a tentative case analysis with no finished statement.
transcription_corrections: Case 1 reads 'Cas α = a′' (not 'α = α′'); case 2 reads 'Cas α = a' — the two cases distinguish matching α with a′ versus a.
'une relation intéressante X → X' is more likely 'une application naturelle 𝒳 → X' (cf. the previous page's 'application naturelle 𝒳 → X').
'l'isom de transition ≃(D) → w(D′)' should read 'ω(D) → ω(D′)'.
'proche d'une pseudo-ligne-lien, D' should read 'proche d'une superposition, D' (the word is hyphenated across lines: 'superposi-tion').
'C'est le cas d'un repère[?]' is probably 'C'est le cas où l'on prend une op. de généralisation en D′ par l'arc qui fait face...'.
'bateau-le-dieu[?]' is uncertain; possibly 'bateau là-dessus' ('I was really led astray on this').
Crossed-out final paragraph approx.: 'Le point de vue de recollements, est mieux en prenant ainsi (pas B1) par B2), et non par A1), et encore, ... point de vue de ..., par A2 ..., dans un dessin'.
